title: Best Home Printers UK
short: Inkjet and ink-tank printers compared by print speed, running cost and features, from occasional-use budget picks to low-cost-per-page tank printers.
intro: A printer's purchase price rarely tells the whole story: cheap cartridge printers can cost far more per page than a pricier ink-tank model over time. This guide compares printers tested by Expert Reviews on speed, print quality and true running costs.

products.name: Pixma TS205
products.best_for: Buyers who only print occasionally and want the simplest, cheapest option
products.key_spec: Thermal inkjet, 4,800 x 1,200dpi, no Wi-Fi or scanner
products.summary: One of the cheapest, simplest printers Expert Reviews has tested, producing bold graphics and crisp black text despite a slightly warm colour bias. It lacks Wi-Fi, a scanner and any smart features, and is slow and noisy, but for occasional print jobs like booking confirmations or family snaps, it's a low-cost, no-fuss option.
pros: Lower ink costs than some pricier printers
Great print quality for the price
cons: No Wi-Fi, scanner or smart features

products.name: OfficeJet Pro 8122e
products.best_for: Buyers who want copy, print, scan and network sharing for under £100
products.key_spec: 225-sheet tray, automatic document feeder, auto duplex printing, colour touchscreen
products.summary: A surprisingly feature-packed all-in-one for the price, with an automatic document feeder, generous paper tray and automatic double-sided printing that budget printers usually skip. Expert Reviews found it better at documents than photos, and ink costs a little more per page than some rivals.
pros: Impressive feature set for the price
Copy, print and scan with Wi-Fi sharing
Automatic document feeder and duplex printing
cons: Higher running costs than tank-based rivals
Photo printing quality is only average

products.name: EcoTank ET-2830
products.badge: Best for fast, cheap home printing
products.best_for: Households that print often and want to avoid buying ink regularly
products.key_spec: Refillable ink tank, 13.4ppm mono, 0.2p per mono page
products.summary: Among the fastest home ink-tank printers Expert Reviews has tested, producing mono prints at 13.4 pages per minute with enough bundled ink for roughly three years of typical printing at just 0.2p per mono page. There's no automatic two-sided printing and the rear paper tray collects dust, but running costs are exceptional.
pros: Very fast for a home ink-tank printer
Bundled ink lasts years of typical use
cons: Rear paper tray prone to collecting dust

products.name: Pixma G650
products.best_for: Buyers who print a lot of photos and want low running costs
products.key_spec: Refillable ink tank, 0.4p mono / 1p colour page cost
products.summary: Combines ink-tank running costs with genuinely good photo output, producing photos on the highest settings that Expert Reviews found almost as good as cartridge-based models. Running costs are impressively low for both mono and colour pages, though print speed is on the slow side.

products.name: Pixma TS8350
products.best_for: Buyers who want the best possible photo print quality at home
products.key_spec: Over 15ppm mono, 10x8in photo prints in under 30 seconds
products.summary: Expert Reviews calls this the versatile home printer to beat, with excellent speed, office-quality text, and some of the best photo prints seen outside a specialist photo printer. Wireless connectivity is rock solid and paper handling is practical, though running costs are high if you print a lot of colour.
pros: Extremely high quality prints, especially photos
Fast print, scan and copy speeds
cons: Expensive to run for high colour volumes
Graphics output can look a little dark

products.name: EcoTank ET-2850
products.best_for: Buyers who want the lowest possible cost per page with core features intact
products.key_spec: Refillable ink tank, auto duplex printing, 0.2p mono / 0.4p colour page cost
products.summary: Sits in the middle of Epson's ink-tank range, keeping automatic duplex printing while shedding extras like fax to keep the price reasonable. Expert Reviews highlights the running costs as the headline feature, with enough bundled ink for 14,000 mono or 5,200 colour pages before you need a refill.
cons: Lacks specialist extras like fax or automatic sheet feeder

products.name: MFC-J4540DW
products.best_for: Buyers who want a full print/scan/copy/fax all-in-one at a reasonable price
products.key_spec: 350-sheet dual paper trays, Wi-Fi/Ethernet, auto duplex, 18.5ppm mono
products.summary: A true all-in-one with print, scan, copy and fax, Wi-Fi or Ethernet connectivity and 350 sheets of paper capacity across two trays. Expert Reviews found print quality solid if just short of the very best, with rapid mono print speeds and comparatively low running costs for a cartridge-based printer.
pros: Large paper capacity across two trays
Comparatively low running costs for cartridges

products.name: OfficeJet Pro 9022e
products.best_for: Buyers who print documents in high volume and want minimal waiting
products.key_spec: 20.5ppm mono, two 250-sheet paper trays, HP Smart app
products.summary: Built for speed, producing mono text documents at a blistering 20.5 pages per minute in Expert Reviews' testing, faster than some laser printers. Easy Wi-Fi or Ethernet sharing via the HP Smart app and two large paper trays suit busy households or small offices, though photo printing isn't its strength.
pros: Easy Wi-Fi/Ethernet setup via HP Smart app

guide.a: Ink-tank (EcoTank/MegaTank-style) printers cost more upfront but bring running costs down to a fraction of a penny per page, paying back the difference within a year or two of regular use. Cartridge printers are cheaper to buy but cost noticeably more per page over time, so they suit only occasional printing.

guide.q: Do I need a scanner and copier, or just printing?
guide.a: If you only ever print documents or photos, a simple printer like the Canon Pixma TS205 here keeps costs down. If you'll also need to scan documents, make copies, or send the occasional fax, an all-in-one (MFP) model is worth the modest extra cost for the convenience.

guide.q: How much does print speed actually matter?
guide.a: For occasional home printing, speed rarely matters much. If you regularly print longer documents or work from home, a faster printer like the HP OfficeJet Pro 9022e here, rated at over 20 pages per minute, saves genuine time compared to budget printers that can be several times slower.

guide.q: Are printers good at photo printing worse at documents?
guide.a: Not necessarily, but there's often a trade-off in running costs. Photo-focused printers like the Canon Pixma TS8350 here produce excellent images but cost more per page for colour printing, while document-focused ink-tank printers prioritise low running costs over the finest photo detail.
